findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, too-long path, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path can abort the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> and propagate with ? or map_err to a typed domain error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on any non-numeric value in the second field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line with non-numeric value aborts the caller instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| RecordError::Parse) or similar typed error, then map_or/ok_or to a domain error

findings.problem: as u16 on a u32 parse result is a lossy cast that silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: a value like 70000 silently becomes 4424, producing corrupt data with no error signal

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses the vector by index without bounds check; a blank line or empty input panics
findings.failure_mode: a single empty line in the file panics the calling thread
findings.fix: use parts.first().copied() or split_once(',') and match the result

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses the vector by index without bounds check; a line with only one field panics
findings.failure_mode: a line missing the second comma panics the calling thread
findings.fix: use parts.get(1) or split_once(',') and match both arms

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side effect (I/O/logging) inside a data-loading function that should be pure parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: hidden I/O side effect in core data logic makes the function non-deterministic from an external observer, breaks referential transparency, and mixes shell concerns into what should be a calculation
findings.fix: remove println! entirely; if logging is needed, return a (Vec<Record>, Vec<String>) or use an explicit logger parameter in the shell layer

findings.problem: Collects all split parts into Vec<String> when only two fields are needed; unnecessary heap allocation per line
findings.failure_mode: allocates a Vec and multiple String heap objects per line instead of reusing or borrowing from the input line
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to get two &str slices directly, avoiding intermediate Vec and per-part allocations

findings.problem: load_samples mixes filesystem I/O (fs::read_to_string) with data parsing; the shell should own I/O and the core should own parsing
findings.failure_mode: the function cannot be tested as pure logic; file-system dependency forces integration tests or mocking for unit coverage
findings.fix: split into shell fn load_samples(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> that reads the file, and pure fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, RecordError> that does parsing

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 instead of domain newtypes; the value field has no domain-level range guarantee at the type level
findings.failure_mode: any code can construct Record { name: "".into(), value: 0 } or value: 99999 via the lossy cast, making illegal states representable at call sites
findings.fix: introduce a value object newtype like struct RecordValue(u16) with a constructor that validates range, and consider a Name newtype if domain rules apply

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_samples throughput or allocation profile
no profiler data (flamegraph, perf, or similar) to validate performance claims
no allocation tracking (e.g., allocative analysis or custom allocator) for the Vec<String> per-line allocation pattern
no second-ring behavior tests (property tests, proptest, or fuzz) for malformed input lines
no command evidence for cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. Multiple BLOCKER findings (unwrap, lossy cast, unchecked indexing, hidden I/O) make the crate unsafe for production use without fixes. The function has no error taxonomy and cannot fail gracefully on any external input.
